_about: References introduced by the process manuals. scripts/manuals_apply.py merges any that are missing into data/references.json (the single bibliography); after that this file is only a record. Public sources only.

references.cite: UC Berkeley Marvell Nanolab, "Run Card for cmos150" (public baseline CMOS process traveler), step 3.0 Well Photo, Mask NWELL (2001).
MicroChemicals GmbH, "Basics of Microstructuring", chapter 1: Fundamentals of Microstructuring (spin coating and softbake).
Willson Research Group, University of Texas at Austin, "Lithography process flow" (post-apply bake, exposure, post-exposure bake and chemical amplification, development) (2002).
University of Kassel, Institute of Nanostructure Technologies and Analytics, "Multilayer Structures for the Lithography in Extreme UV (EUVL)" (typically 40 Mo/Si bilayers, reflectivity up to 70 %).

BYU Integrated Microfabrication Lab, "RIE" (Anelva DEM-451 parallel-plate 13.56 MHz reactive ion etcher: CF₄/O₂ for Si, Si₃N₄ and SiO₂; pump to 20 mTorr or less; pressure rises 20–40 mTorr when RF is on).
UCSB Nanofabrication Facility wiki, "RIE 1 (Custom)" (chlorine reactive ion etcher at 13.56 MHz; GaAs at 2 mTorr Cl₂, 350 V bias, about 200 nm/min).
Wikipedia, "Reactive-ion etching" (pressure a few mTorr to a few hundred mTorr; 13.56 MHz at a few hundred watts; DC self-bias of a few hundred volts; ICP sources; deep RIE).

Compugraphics Photomasks, "Education centre: what is a photomask?" (fused-silica or soda-lime substrates with an opaque film; write, develop, etch, measure, inspect, repair, pellicle; 5 to 40+ masks per device).

S. Cargou, "Fabrication of glass and film photomasks," Elveflow microfluidic reviews (2022, updated 2025) (chrome blank with anti-reflective coating and resist; laser writer with micromirror array, 0.8 µm pixels).
Wikipedia, "Photomask" (chromium on fused silica; 4× or 5× reduction; phase shifting below about 150 nm; pellicles; reflective Mo/Si EUV masks; mask costs).
Wikipedia, "Chemical-mechanical polishing" (abrasive slurry, porous polymer pads with 30–50 µm pores, use for oxide, tungsten and copper, STI overburden, defects).
